column1: # mutation-operators.tsv — the generic mutant operators swept over every paired guard.
# TAB-separated. Columns:
#   id <TAB> match <TAB> flip
# id     A stable token. It is BYTE-COMPARED inside generic survivor ids
#        (`<guard relpath>::<id>::<key>`), so renaming an id re-keys every survivor it
#        produced. One id per textual mutation — never a prose "family".
# match  The site-enumerating ERE, applied with `grep -nE --` (the option terminator is
#        load-bearing: a match may begin with a hyphen, and a match grep cannot run as a
#        pattern is a named red, never a silent zero-site pass). A SITE IS A MATCHED LINE
#        THAT IS NOT A COMMENT: at most one mutation per line per operator, and lines
#        matching `^[[:space:]]*#` are dropped from the matched-line list BEFORE anything
#        is counted (#579). A site's IDENTITY is its content, not its place in that list
#        (#583): `<key>` is 12 hex of a sha256 over the whitespace-normalized matched line
#        plus its occurrence index among the operator's normalization-identical matched
#        lines in the same guard. So raising the per-guard budget K re-keys nothing, adding
#        or deleting a COMMENT re-keys nothing, inserting a killable line above a site
#        re-keys nothing, and MOVING a block — indentation changed or not — re-keys nothing.
#        An ordinary guard edit therefore carries NO re-baseline obligation. Only editing a
#        site's own line, or removing one of its normalization-identical siblings from
#        earlier in the file, changes a key.
#        The exclusion is not an optimization. A comment flip changes no reachable
#        behavior, so no suite can kill it: every comment site was a permanent baseline
#        row, and at k=2 they routinely took ordinals 1 and 2 and pushed the real code
#        sites out of the swept window — a green sweep then proved count and labels, never
#        identity. It is LEADING `#` only: a trailing comment on a code line still
#        enumerates (the matches are substring EREs), and `#`-headed heredoc payload stops
#        enumerating with it. Both residues are accepted; see docs/testing.md.
# flip   The sed -E program applied to that ONE line. Two-way swaps route through the
#        placeholder __MUT__ so the program is not self-cancelling (a naive
#        `s/-eq/-ne/; s/-ne/-eq/` restores the original).
# Editing a `match` regex changes WHICH lines are sites, so it can drop rows sweep-wide and,
# where it removes a normalization-identical sibling, re-key the ones that followed it. It no
# longer re-keys an operator's whole set: the sites it leaves matching keep their keys.
# An operator with no applicable site in a guard is NORMAL: it contributes no mutants.
# Non-application is data, never red. (15 of the 34 same-stem-paired guards contain no
# literal `exit 1`, so `fail-open` alone is inapplicable to roughly a third of them.)
# An operator whose matched lines were ALL comments is a DIFFERENT normal state, and the
# report says which: the `sites_comment_only` column names it per operator rather than
# emitting the same silence as no-applicable-site. Also data, also never red.
# A generic mutant that fails `bash -n` is a HARNESS ARTIFACT: skipped and logged, never
# red. Only CATALOG mutants red on validity (that is anchor drift). The tiers are
# deliberately asymmetric — generic sites are machine-enumerated and may land somewhere a
# blind sed cannot express, whereas a catalog row is hand-authored against a named site.
fail-open
cmp-eq
